title: Storm Eels Lomax Salary Cap: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the 38-hour week, including the storm eels lomax salary cap example. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52-week year, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour, equating to $1004.90 per week or $52,254.80 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee on a 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour yields $52,254.80 per year. Always check your award or agreement, as some have different weekly hours.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44/hour from 1 July 2026) applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates, penalty rates, and allowances. For example, the General Retail Industry Award or Restaurant Industry Award have specific pay rates. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool or pay guides to find the correct rate for your job.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied, and does it affect annual conversion?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, intended to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05/hour ($26.44 + 25%). When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate if you are a casual employee. However, super is calculated on the base rate (ordinary time earnings), not the loaded amount. Always check your award for specific casual loading rules.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

Understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential whether you're negotiating a salary, budgeting, or checking compliance. The standard full-time week in Australia is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. This article uses that assumption to walk you through the conversion, including tax, superannuation, and the differences between the National Minimum Wage and award rates. We'll also touch on the hypothetical "storm eels lomax salary cap" as an example of how these calculations apply to any reported salary figure.

## The 38-Hour Week and Annual Conversion

The basic formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, this becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

Using the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026, set by the Fair Work Commission at $26.44 per hour, the calculation is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year

This matches the weekly rate of $1,004.90 (38 × $26.44) multiplied by 52. The same formula works for any hourly rate. For example, if you hear about the "storm eels lomax salary cap" – a hypothetical figure often discussed in rugby league circles – you can convert it back to an hourly rate by dividing the annual amount by (38 × 52).

Remember: this assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If your award specifies different hours (e.g., 35 or 40 hours), adjust accordingly. Always refer to your [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) for exact figures.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two:

**Weekly pay × 2**

Using the National Minimum Wage example:

$1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight

This is useful for budgeting and comparing with salary offers that are quoted fortnightly. The same logic applies: if you have an annual salary, divide by 26 to get the fortnightly amount.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44/hour) applies only to employees who are not covered by an award or registered agreement. Most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For instance, the General Retail Industry Award and Restaurant Industry Award have specific classifications with different pay levels. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing minimum hourly rates, penalty rates, and allowances.

Award rates often exceed the National Minimum Wage. For example, a Level 1 retail employee may earn more than $26.44 per hour. Always check your award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool. If you are award-free, the National Minimum Wage is your floor.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is:

$26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour

When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate if you are casual. However, superannuation is calculated on ordinary time earnings – the base rate, not the loaded amount. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this in more detail.

If you use our [the timesheet](/) tool, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

## Tax and Super

### Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The tax-free threshold is built into these rates. For the National Minimum Wage annual income of $52,254.80, the tax would be approximately:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $7,254.80 ($45,001 to $52,254.80) = $2,176.44
- Total tax ≈ $6,196.44
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,254.80) ≈ $1,045.10
- Total deductions ≈ $7,241.54

This leaves an after-tax annual income of about $45,013.26. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed calculator.

### Superannuation

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% on ordinary time earnings, on top of your salary. For the National Minimum Wage:

$52,254.80 × 12% = $6,270.58 per year

This is paid into your super fund and is not part of your take-home pay. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## Example: Storm Eels Lomax Salary Cap

Let's apply the conversion to a hypothetical salary cap figure. Suppose the "storm eels lomax salary cap" is reported as $800,000 per year. To find the hourly rate (assuming a 38-hour week, 52 weeks):

$800,000 ÷ (38 × 52) = $800,000 ÷ 1,976 ≈ $404.86 per hour

This is a high rate, typical of professional athletes. The same formula works in reverse: if you know the hourly rate, multiply by 1,976 to get annual. This example shows how the conversion applies to any salary, from minimum wage to executive levels.

## Conclusion

Converting hourly rates to annual pay is straightforward with the 38-hour week assumption. Always verify your award or agreement for exact hours and rates. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's tools and our [reference tables](/data) for accurate figures. Remember that tax, Medicare, and super are additional considerations that affect your net income. Whether you're checking the National Minimum Wage or a hypothetical "storm eels lomax salary cap", the math remains the same.
